Ranking quality across queries

MethodnDCG@10 ↑Δ currentP@10 ↑Mean coverage ↑Top-1 coverage ↑Queries

nDCG@10: coverage-weighted ranking quality relative to the best possible order of this corpus (1 is best). P@10: fraction of the top ten with at least 10% measured coverage for every requested color. For several colors, graded “coverage” is the aggregate presence score. The default palette method was selected using development queries.

How to read this experiment
  • CIELAB D65 measurements count alpha-weighted pixels within distance 20, 30, or 40 of the requested color. They use a separate, higher-resolution sample and no candidate histogram or palette.
  • The HSV proxy uses hue difference ≤25°, saturation and value differences ≤0.3. Grayscale queries use pixel saturation <0.15 and value difference ≤0.2.
  • Multi-color relevance is the amount-weighted geometric mean of individual coverages; a missing color produces zero. This describes color presence rather than composition.
  • Thresholds and the development / holdout split were fixed before evaluating rankings. Comparing many alternatives still makes this an exploratory benchmark.
  • Exact OpenSearch searches compare all 100 candidates; native ANN checks are recorded in the raw data. Application palette scores are also evaluated over all 100. A production reranker would depend on candidate recall.
  • Recorded run times include experiment overhead. They are not production latency measurements, and 100 images cannot establish performance at scale.
